intro: Picture waking up, pulling back the curtain to a quiet stretch of the Gulf of Thailand in an old fishing neighbourhood, taking a few steps to pay your respects at Wat Ang Sila, then sitting down to a breakfast of fresh seafood from Ang Sila Market — Central Place Serviced Apartment Angsila is a budget seaside serviced apartment in Ang Sila, Mueang Chonburi district, that leans on one simple, honest selling point: it offers sea-view rooms with balconies starting from a few hundred to just over a thousand baht · This is not a luxury resort, there is no swimming pool, and it is a small building of around 20 rooms that has been open since 2015, but the location is what many guests rate as its biggest strength, within walking distance of Ang Sila's temple, market and waterfront · Prices start at around ฿700/night · It scores 8.7 overall from 53 reviews on Trip.com, with location rated as high as 9.6, and Tripadvisor ranks it #1 among B&B/Inn stays in Ang Sila

body.html: Overview and who it suits — To put it as simply as possible, Central Place Serviced Apartment Angsila is a stay for people who want a "seaside room for a few hundred baht" in the middle of Chonburi's old fishing community, rather than a resort with a pool and full facilities · It is a 2-star serviced apartment, open since 2015, set in Ang Sila in Mueang Chonburi district, an area known for fresh seafood, the Ang Sila stone mortar, and a quiet seaside way of life that is calmer than Bang Saen · The building is small, with only around 20 rooms, which gives it a friendly, uncrowded feel compared with a big hotel · Real reviews line up on who fits here: budget travellers who want to stay by the sea, couples on a short trip who are not chasing luxury, people in town on business or work around Chonburi-Ang Sila, and anyone who comes specifically to eat seafood and experience the Ang Sila community · On the other hand, if you are after a resort with a swimming pool, a sandy beach you can swim from, or full hotel-style facilities, this may not be the answer, and you should look at stays around Bang Saen or Pattaya instead · In short, Central Place sells location, quiet and a sea view on a very reachable budget, rather than luxury or a long list of facilities, which is why its value and location scores sit on the high side

Location and getting around — This is without question the number-one selling point here, and the area that scores highest in real reviews at 9.6 out of 10 · The stay sits at 100/12 Moo 1, Ang Sila subdistrict, on the waterfront of the Ang Sila community · The advantage of this location is that you can walk to almost everything important in the area — Wat Ang Sila is only about 170 metres away, Ang Sila Market and the fish pier that sell fresh seafood and the famous stone mortars are a roughly 5–10 minute walk, and the King's Tribute Museum is nearby · There is a convenience store such as 7-Eleven and a retail store such as Lotus's close by, making it easy to pick up food and supplies · For longer trips, the busier Bang Saen Beach is about 6 kilometres, or roughly a 10–15 min drive, and central Chonburi is a short drive away · Suvarnabhumi Airport is about 90–100 kilometres away, and the stay offers an airport transfer you can ask about · One thing the reviews say plainly: Ang Sila is a community where public transport is limited, with an area-wide walkability score of around 40 out of 100, so if you want to go beyond the community itself, having your own car or renting a motorbike is the most convenient option, and there is free parking here to support that
"The room was very clean, a few-hundred-baht price but a thousand-baht view, genuinely worth it. Easy walk to Wat Ang Sila and the market, and you wake up, open the curtain, and there's the sea."

Room types and decor — Central Place is a small building of around 20 rooms, split into several types by bed size and view · The main options are the Standard Double Room with one large bed for couples or solo guests, the Standard Twin Room with two single beds for friends or family, the Standard Twin Room with Balcony which adds a private balcony, and the one most people are after, the Standard Room with Double Bed and Sea View, a large-bed room with a sea view · The decor is simple and easy on the eye, focused on being practical rather than luxurious, and every room has air conditioning, cable TV (with English channels), a phone, a sitting corner, and an en-suite bathroom with basic amenities and towels · Most real reviews praise the rooms as clean, roomier than expected for the price, comfortable to sleep in, and in a building that still looks new, and many are surprised by the sea view relative to what they paid · But to be straight with you, there are a few things worth knowing — some reviews say certain fittings are starting to age and some in-room items are not fully stocked, for example some rooms have no kettle, and the bathroom amenities are budget grade · The view also varies by room type, so if a sea view matters to you, book a Sea View room directly from the start, because a standard room may not have a full view of the sea

Facilities and pool — To be straight from the start, Central Place has no swimming pool, a limitation worth knowing before you book, because it positions itself as a budget serviced apartment, not a resort · The facilities it does have focus on what is enough for the stay — there is free Wi-Fi in the common areas, free parking in the building, an airport transfer service (ask ahead), luggage storage, laundry and dry cleaning, and daily housekeeping · There is a shared kitchen in the building for guests to cook or reheat food, which fits the serviced-apartment concept for longer stays · Some sources note it is a family-friendly stay with a little space for children · The real selling point here is not the number of facilities but the location within walking distance of Ang Sila's temple, market and waterfront, paired with budget sea-view rooms · For people planning to use the stay as a base for eating seafood and strolling along the water, this is a set of facilities that matches how you will actually use it · But for anyone who wants a pool, a gym, a spa or in-house activities, you have to accept that this place cannot provide them, and you should look for a resort at a higher budget

Food and places to eat nearby — Central Place is a budget stay that generally does not include breakfast in the room rate, unlike a hotel with a buffet, but that is no problem at all for an Ang Sila location, because this is one of Chonburi's most famous seafood neighbourhoods · A few minutes' walk from the stay you reach Ang Sila Market and the fish pier, selling fresh seafood at local prices — shrimp, shellfish, crab, fish — along with local snacks and made-to-order eateries · Many reviews say it is very easy to find food around the stay, with waterfront restaurants, cafes and convenience stores · For those who want to cook, the shared kitchen helps, especially if you buy fresh seafood from the market to cook yourself · Ang Sila's edge is that the food is good and cheap, so there is no need to rely on food at the stay · Overall, food at Central Place is not the reason to come for what is served on site, but it is a location that puts Ang Sila's fresh seafood within walking distance, which many see as a charm rather than a drawback

Service and staff — Service is another area that earns fairly consistent praise in real reviews, scoring around 8.6 out of 10 · Many say the staff are friendly and helpful, and offer good information about getting around and where to eat in the area · There is luggage storage and an airport transfer that help a lot with travel, since Ang Sila has limited public transport · For balance, a few reviews note that cancellation and refund handling in some cases was not as smooth as it should have been, with one review giving a low score because they did not get a refund for a cancelled trip, so read the booking conditions carefully before paying · Overall, service is still a strength here and one of the reasons the review scores sit at a good level

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — Pulled together from Trip.com, Tripadvisor and other review sources, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: a great location within walking distance of Ang Sila's temple, market and waterfront (the highest-scoring area at 9.6), clean rooms that are roomier than expected, a sea view many describe as "a few-hundred-baht price but a thousand-baht view," comfortable beds, a building that still looks new, friendly and helpful staff, and easy access close to a convenience store · On the watch-out side: the points raised are that there is no swimming pool and it is a budget stay with no breakfast, soundproofing between rooms is not great with some people clearly hearing the door of the room next door opening and closing, certain fittings are starting to age and some in-room items are not fully stocked, for example some rooms have no kettle and the bathroom amenities are budget grade, and there is a review that gripes about a refund on cancellation · Most of these gripes are about setting your expectations to match a few-hundred-baht price and being fine with that, rather than being a big problem, because the overall score still sits at 8.7 and many say it is worth it and they would come back

"The room was clean and comfortable, the location made it easy to walk anywhere, great value for a short stay · The only downside is you hear a bit of noise from the room next door, and some in-room items are not fully stocked, but if you know what to expect going in, it's fine."

Price comparison and value — Nightly rates start at around ฿700/night for a Standard room on a weekday, moving up to roughly ฿900–฿1,400 for a sea-view room or during long weekends and festivals when Ang Sila-Bang Saen gets busy · What makes Central Place good value is that you get a clean room in a building that still looks new, with the chance of a sea view and a balcony, at a guesthouse-level price, which is hard to find in a seaside location · Compared with a seaside stay on the Bang Saen side such as BBG Seaside, which has larger rooms and a kitchen in every room but rates moving up into the two thousands, or a design-led stay such as Kalm Bangsaen, which is attractive and has a pool but costs more, Central Place clearly wins on price and a location in the heart of the Ang Sila community, but loses on room size, pool and facilities · In short, if you put weight on a tight budget, an Ang Sila seaside location, and a sea view for a few hundred baht, every baht you spend feels well returned, especially for a short one- to two-night stay

What to know before booking — A few things help the stay go smoothly · One, there is no swimming pool and no breakfast here, so if you want those, consider a resort-type stay · Two, if a sea view matters to you, book a Sea View room or a room with a balcony directly from the start, because a standard room may not see the sea · Three, soundproofing between rooms is not great, so if you are a light sleeper bring earplugs or ask for a room away from busy areas · Four, some in-room items may not be fully stocked, such as a kettle, so if you need one, ask or bring your own · Five, Ang Sila has limited public transport, so if you do not have your own car, plan your travel ahead, for example renting a motorbike or using a ride-hailing service, and there is free parking for those who drive themselves · Six, read the cancellation and refund conditions carefully before paying, and choose free cancellation if your plans are not yet firm · Seven, during long weekends Ang Sila-Bang Saen gets crowded, rooms are few and sell out fast, so book ahead and compare prices across several platforms

Summary — From everything the real reviews say, Central Place Serviced Apartment Angsila is the best fit for people who want a clean seaside room, with the chance of a sea view and a balcony, on a budget of a few hundred baht, in the heart of the Ang Sila community within walking distance of the temple, market and fresh seafood · A location scoring as high as 9.6, clean rooms, a building that still looks new, and a sea view at a reachable price make it good value for budget travellers, couples on a short trip, and people who come specifically to eat seafood and experience the Ang Sila community · But you have to accept honestly that there is no swimming pool, no breakfast, soundproofing between rooms is not great, some in-room items are not fully stocked, and the area is most convenient to get around when you have a car · If you are looking for a resort with a pool, large rooms with a kitchen in every room, or full facilities, this may not be the answer, and you should look at options on the Bang Saen or Pattaya side instead · But for an easy-on-the-wallet seaside trip where you want a location in the heart of Ang Sila and a sea view for a few hundred baht — Central Place answers that need well, and it is why it holds a top spot among stays of this kind in Ang Sila

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Central Place Serviced Apartment Angsila

faq.q: Where is Central Place Angsila, and what can you walk to?
faq.a: The stay sits at 100/12 Moo 1, Ang Sila subdistrict, Mueang Chonburi district, on the waterfront of the Ang Sila community · You can walk to Wat Ang Sila, about 170 metres away, and Ang Sila Market-fish pier, which sells fresh seafood, in about 5–10 minutes · The King's Tribute Museum and Ang Sila Old Market are nearby · Bang Saen Beach is about 6 kilometres, or a 10–15 min drive, away

faq.q: Does Central Place Angsila have a swimming pool and breakfast?
faq.a: There is no swimming pool, and breakfast is generally not included, because it is a budget serviced apartment · But the location is in the heart of Ang Sila's seafood neighbourhood, a few minutes' walk to the market and waterfront restaurants · There is a shared kitchen in the building for cooking your own meals · If you want a pool and a breakfast buffet, look at resort-type stays on the Bang Saen or Pattaya side

faq.q: What is the starting price at Central Place Angsila, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around ฿700/night for a Standard room on a weekday · There are Twin rooms, rooms with a balcony, and a Sea View room with a large bed and a sea view, where the price moves up to roughly ฿900–฿1,400 · If you want a sea view, book a Sea View room directly from the start · Rooms sell out fast on long weekends, so compare several platforms before booking

faq.q: Who is Central Place Angsila best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for budget travellers, couples on a short trip, and people who come specifically to eat seafood and experience the Ang Sila community and want a clean seaside room on a budget of a few hundred baht · It's not a fit for people who want a resort with a swimming pool, a sandy beach you can swim from, or full big-hotel facilities, who should look at the Bang Saen or Pattaya side instead

faq.q: What are the noise and in-room amenities like at Central Place Angsila?
faq.a: Some reviews say soundproofing between rooms is not great, with the door of the room next door clearly heard opening and closing, so if you're a light sleeper, bring earplugs or ask for a room away from busy areas · And some in-room items may not be fully stocked, for example some rooms have no kettle and the bathroom amenities are budget grade, so if you need them, ask or bring your own

faq.q: Is it convenient to reach Central Place Angsila without a car?
faq.a: Ang Sila has limited public transport, with an area-wide walkability score of around 40 out of 100 · The stay itself is an easy walk to the temple, market and sea, but if you want to go beyond the community, such as to Bang Saen Beach or central Chonburi, having your own car is the most convenient · The stay has free parking and an airport transfer · If you don't have a car, plan to rent a motorbike or use a ride-hailing service
